title: Strong monoidal functors and their structure maps
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be monoidal categories [def-sfb-monoidal-category], with unit objects $\mathbf1_{\mathcal C},\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}$, associators $\alpha^{\mathcal C},\alpha^{\mathcal D}$ and unitors $\lambda^{\mathcal C},\rho^{\mathcal C},\lambda^{\mathcal D},\rho^{\mathcal D}$.
A strong monoidal structure on a functor $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ consists of an isomorphism
$e:\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}\xrightarrow{\sim}F\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}$ and isomorphisms
$\mu_{X,Y}:FX\otimes FY\xrightarrow{\sim}F(X\otimes Y)$ natural in $X,Y$.
Writing $e,\mu$ also for their forward morphisms, they satisfy, for all $X,Y,Z\in\mathcal C$,
$$
F(\alpha^{\mathcal C}_{X,Y,Z})\circ\mu_{X\otimes Y,Z}\circ(\mu_{X,Y}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{FZ})
=\mu_{X,Y\otimes Z}\circ(\mathrm{id}_{FX}\otimes\mu_{Y,Z})\circ\alpha^{\mathcal D}_{FX,FY,FZ},
$$
$$
F(\lambda^{\mathcal C}_X)\circ\mu_{\mathbf1_{\mathcal C},X}\circ(e\otimes\mathrm{id}_{FX})=\lambda^{\mathcal D}_{FX},\qquad
F(\rho^{\mathcal C}_X)\circ\mu_{X,\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}}\circ(\mathrm{id}_{FX}\otimes e)=\rho^{\mathcal D}_{FX}.
$$
An isomorphism is a morphism with a specified two-sided inverse; the inverse structure maps are $\mu_{X,Y}^{-1}$ and $e^{-1}$. No braiding or symmetry is required.
Here a functor assigns objects and morphisms preserving identities and composition. Naturality of the tensorator means that for morphisms $f:X\to X'$ and $g:Y\to Y'$,
$$F(f\otimes g)\circ\mu_{X,Y}=\mu_{X',Y'}\circ(F(f)\otimes F(g)).$$
